outcomes: Reproduce a serial gradient update with communicating data-parallel workers
Trace tensor-sharded forward and backward reductions
Send activations forward and gradients backward through two pipeline stages
Resume minibatch training from validated state and explain the limits of equivalence
lessons: Why one worker stops being enough

data-parallelism.name: Data parallelism
data-parallelism.definition: Replicating a model while assigning different examples to workers.
data-parallelism.explanation: Each worker evaluates the same parameter values on a different slice of the batch and produces a local gradient sum. A collective combines those sums, using example counts when slices are uneven, before every replica applies the same update. The approach increases throughput when computation outweighs communication. It does not change the mathematical full-batch objective when reductions and scaling agree, although floating-point reduction order can change the final low bits.

tensor-parallelism.name: Tensor parallelism
tensor-parallelism.definition: Partitioning one tensor operation across workers.
tensor-parallelism.explanation: A matrix or dot product can be split by rows or columns so each worker owns only part of the parameters and arithmetic. The local results are incomplete until a mathematically required communication combines them. The chapter splits a four-feature dot product into two parameter shards, sums their partial activations, computes one shared residual, and routes gradient components back to the owning shards. Real accelerator systems apply the same idea at far larger scale.

pipeline-parallelism.name: Pipeline parallelism
pipeline-parallelism.definition: Placing consecutive model stages on different workers.
pipeline-parallelism.explanation: The first stage sends activations to the next stage during the forward pass. The later stage sends activation gradients in the reverse direction during backpropagation. Dividing a batch into microbatches can keep several stages busy, though filling and draining the pipeline creates idle bubbles. The local project uses two CPU threads and typed channels to expose both directions while freezing the stage parameters until the complete minibatch gradient has been collected.

checkpoint-recovery.name: Checkpoint recovery
checkpoint-recovery.definition: Restoring all state needed to continue an interrupted computation.
checkpoint-recovery.explanation: A useful training checkpoint includes parameters, optimizer state when present, progress counters, and the data or random cursor that determines the next update. The chapter serializes a versioned model, step, and minibatch cursor, reloads them, and compares the next result with uninterrupted training. This demonstrates deterministic recovery for the local fixture. Distributed hardware, different reduction trees, or nondeterministic kernels can still prevent bitwise reproduction across environments.

sources.title: PyTorch Distributed Data Parallel design note

checks: Data-parallel steps match serial steps within 1e-12 for batch sizes 1, 3, and 5
Tensor-parallel prediction and parameter update match the serial reference within 1e-12
Two-stage pipeline backward matches serial and finite-difference gradients for three- and four-example data slices
Empty or nonfinite pipeline data, invalid learning rates, and nonfinite updates are rejected
CH50v1 parameter order and cursor bytes remain stable, and a restored two-minibatch run equals the uninterrupted local run
Malformed and nonfinite checkpoints are rejected
limitations: Threads and channels verify local CPU communication, not multi-GPU execution or network collectives
The checkpoint demo round-trips a serialized string in one process; it does not persist to disk, relaunch, or implement automatic worker failure detection
Floating-point equivalence is tolerance-based across different reduction orders and hardware
